messages:
eva_ops: seeing recurring p99 tail spikes on eu-west GPU pods, looks correlated with NIC tx drops and gpu_util oscillation. started ~03:40UTC and hit two times in the last hour. :frowning_face:
michael_s: nice catch — do we have a tenant or workload that lines up? any noisy neighbour hints? :eyes:
sophia_p: quick query: 
```
sum(rate(node_network_transmit_packets_dropped_total{device=~"eth.*"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
returns a couple of instances with bursts at the same time as p99 spikes. attaching grafana snapshot in thread.
ravi_k: my hunch: NIC queue saturation -> kernel scheduling jitter -> NVML reports gpu_util thrashing -> inference latency spikes. we've seen this when multi-tenant tenants share pcie root and host NIC without SR-IOV/QoS.
jeamie_d: can we short-term route the suspected tenants to dedicated pools? we have soft-reserve pools for premium customers but not for small heavy-burst tenants. tradeoffs: capacity cost vs 50–200ms p99 reduction.
eva_ops: (typo) — jamie_d: agreed. can we create a temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated-gpu-pool for tenants:tenantburst=true ? something like: 
```
routing_policy:
  - match: tenant.labels.burst == "true"
    prefer_pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-west
    fallback: shared-gpu-pool
    max_burst_tokens: 5
```
will that be enforced at the proxy level?
michael_s: infra-proxy can apply tag-based routing today, but we need to verify capacity headroom in eu-west. ops-sim shows ~20% headroom if we drop noncritical jobs. cost hit ~+8% for the cluster for 3 hours.
sophia_p: small patch to check in metrics alerting: add node_network_transmit_packets_dropped_total > 0 for 3/5 windows to trigger early. currently we only alert on gpu latency.
ravi_k: longer-term fix: enable SR-IOV + dedicated VF pools for heavy-tenants + tweak kernel txq linearization. also consider enabling soft kernel preemption (CONFIG_PREEMPT_VOLUNTARY) on our internal AMI to reduce long IRQ hold times. that combined with cgroup v2 net_cls QoS should help. note: kernel tweak needs canary run — may affect throughput slightly.
jamie_d: ops: create canary on 2 nodes in eu-west, schedule the offending tenant there and compare p50/p95/p99. If good, roll to a set of 10% nodes. I can own rollout steps.
infra-bot: alert created: CID-2026-1001 NIC_DROP_BURST eu-west, triggered at 1765432100 by eva_ops. linked runbook: /runbooks/networking/nic-queue-saturation.md
eva_ops: thanks. i'll queue a routing rule PR and add the grafana links. also tagging @oncall for awareness. :thumbsup:
